topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This topic introduces the cancer lecture series and outlines the core learning outcomes on environmental exposures, carcinogenicity, and tumor development.

topics.label: Cancer etiology, endogenous mutation, and epidemiological evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental causes of cancer, contrasting intrinsic cell-biological processes with environmental exposures through public perception and global epidemiological variation.

topics.label: Pathogens and oncogenesis: viral, bacterial, and co-infection mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological agents such as bacteria, parasites, and viruses contribute to cancer development, highlighting the interaction between Epstein-Barr virus and malaria in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens: metabolic activation and DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how environmental agents, radiation, and dietary compounds undergo xenobiotic metabolism to form DNA adducts and induce genetic mutations.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, inflammatory microenvironments, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic mechanisms of tumorigenesis, examining how chronic inflammation, promotional signals like phorbol esters, and host developmental windows drive tumor development.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens, mutational signatures, and assessing risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the experimental, genomic, and epidemiological methods used to establish carcinogenicity and conclude with practical risk-benefit considerations.
